name: Sable Noir Lemongrass-Burnt Caramel Tablets
description: Thin-pressed synth-dark tablets with a real lemongrass oil infusion and a scorched caramel layer that cracks audibly. No real cocoa, but the roasted synth-base mimics dark chocolate character convincingly.
flavor_profile: Bright citrus-herb lemongrass top note, deep burnt caramel body, dry roasted finish with faint smoke
cultural_context: Sable Noir's tablet line is a status object for Tier 3 consumers who want to signal taste without Tier 4 spending. The burnt caramel variant is considered the most sophisticated in the line and is frequently gifted at professional milestone events as a subtle flex.
story_hooks: Sable Noir's 'real lemongrass oil' is actually a biosynthesized compound indistinguishable from the real thing — which makes their premium pricing a legal gray area that a consumer advocacy group is about to expose.

A Tier 4 executive insists on Sable Noir tablets at every board meeting; when a rival sends a counterfeit batch, the executive's reaction reveals how much she relies on the ritual for psychological stability.
The scorched caramel technique was developed by a the Gray Zone chemist who sold the formula to Sable Noir for rent money and now watches her invention sold at ten times what she earned from it.
